title: API Schema/Documentation Publicly Exposed (65.61.137.117:443)
description: API schema or documentation endpoints are publicly accessible: /?wsdl(200) /?WSDL(200) . This exposes full API surface, endpoint parameters, and authentication mechanisms to attackers.
recommendation: Restrict schema endpoints behind authentication. Remove swagger/openapi files from production or gate behind IP allowlisting.

title: Missing Rate Limiting on Login/Auth Endpoint (65.61.137.117:443)
description: No rate limiting or throttling detected at https://65.61.137.117:443/api/login. 10 rapid authentication requests were accepted without restriction. This enables brute-force attacks (OWASP API4).
recommendation: Implement rate limiting (e.g., 5 req/min per IP on auth endpoints). Add CAPTCHA after failed attempts. Deploy account lockout after N failures. Use token bucket or sliding window algorithms.

title: Server Version Disclosure in Response Headers (65.61.137.117:443)
description: The Server response header reveals software version: Server: Apache-Coyote/1.1. This aids attackers in identifying vulnerable versions.
recommendation: Configure web server to suppress or genericize the Server header (ServerTokens Prod for Apache; server_tokens off for Nginx).

title: Missing Security Response Headers (65.61.137.117:443)
description: The following security headers are absent from https://65.61.137.117:443: Permissions-Policy; Referrer-Policy; Strict-Transport-Security; X-Content-Type-Options; X-XSS-Protection; X-Frame-Options; Cache-Control; Content-Security-Policy; . Each missing header increases attack surface for XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and information disclosure.
recommendation: Implement all recommended security headers. Use a Content Security Policy builder to create strict CSP. Enable HSTS with includeSubDomains and preload. Refer to OWASP Secure Headers Project.
